newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech house extends cabinet confidence vote debate.
newsitem.headline: Czech house extends cabinet confidence vote debate.

text.p: The lower house of the Czech parliament agreed to suspend its rules and extend Tuesday's debate on a vote of confidence in the cabinet until 11 p.m. (2100 gmt).
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus asked the house for the confidence vote as his government tries to implement a series of austerity measures to stabilise a sagging economy and bolster the Czech crown.
Deputies also voted to allow a final vote to be taken, if debate ends, until 9 p.m. Normally, house rules require any vote to be taken before 7 p.m. local time.
Debate on the confidence vote can resume beyond Tuesday if it is not completed.
The ruling coalition controls 100 votes in the 200-seat house for the confidence vote which requires a simple majority of those voting for approval.

Analysts expect at least 97 opposition deputies to vote against the government, but the voting intentions of the two unaffiliated deputies were unclear and one deputy from the Communist party has said he is unable to vote for health reasons.
Debate continued throughout the afternoon reflecting traditional party lines, but it was not clear when a final vote might be taken.
